findings: The frozen repository context contains two equivalent MySQL index-access questions and explicitly names both implicit conversion and the leftmost-prefix rule. The candidate answers both variants directly and covers those required entities in the core, one-minute, three-minute and follow-up sections.

The MySQL 8.4 primary-source packet supports the candidate's central two-layer model: a predicate can fail to form the desired B-Tree lookup/range, or an index can remain usable while the cost-based optimizer selects a scan or another access path instead.

The composite-index discussion is appropriately qualified. It explains ordinary leftmost-prefix access while preserving Skip Scan as a documented exception boundary, avoiding the hard-failure pattern of turning an interview mnemonic into an exception-free optimizer law.

The implicit-conversion section matches the documented indexed-string-versus-numeric-value case and correctly frames parameter/column type compatibility as part of indexability rather than treating conversion as a cosmetic SQL issue.

The candidate correctly distinguishes constant-prefix LIKE from leading-wildcard LIKE, expression/index matching from the false 'functions always disable indexes' rule, and range-interval construction from the broader usefulness of later composite-index columns.

The answer gives cost/selectivity/statistics their own causal layer and requires EXPLAIN, with EXPLAIN ANALYZE when actual execution data is appropriate, instead of declaring index use from keyword rules alone. It also avoids fabricated production incidents or performance numbers.

A few illustrative optimizer details such as later-column filtering/coverage examples are broader than the frozen claim anchors, so facts-and-evidence is scored 24/25 rather than perfect. They do not change the core conclusion or create an unsupported material claim. The one-minute section has six numbered points rather than the preferred three-to-five, and the three-minute section is longer than literal oral timing, so oral quality is scored 4/5 and type-specific completeness 19/20.
